identity.name: Gothia
alt_names: Gothic realm north of the Black Sea

land.text: the Wielbark Goths of the Vistula and Bug, who moved to the Black Sea steppe

predecessors.note: The Goths page has the Wielbark culture shift 'southeast towards the Black Sea' from the middle of the 2nd century; the 206/207 boundary is Cliopatria's.

land.text: the Danubian lands in Scythia (Minor), Moesia and Thrace on which the Goths were settled as foederati by the peace of 3 October 382

successors.note: 'The Goths recognized the authority of the Roman emperor and were nominally incorporated into the Roman Empire' (Gothic War page). The Roman Empire row of Cliopatria ends 394; the Eastern Roman Empire's row opens 395.

land.text: the Pontic steppe (375) and the plains north of the Lower Danube (376), taken by the Huns before the end

successors.note: The Hunnic gains of 373-376 are dated in the ledger; the huns dossier of this batch carries the matching gains (it dates the steppe 375).

keyframe_review.note: 210,831 km2, 207-237: Podolia, eastern Moldova and Bessarabia and part of Volhynia between the Dniester and the Dnieper. unverified for these years: no page opened dates a Gothic realm here before 238 (the first Gothic incursion, the sack of Histria); the Goths page has Wielbark Goths 'probably in Roman service' 'by 200 AD' and contributing to the Chernyakhov culture 'by the mid-3rd century', and the Chernyakhov page has that culture 'flourished between the 2nd and 5th centuries' in Ukraine, Romania and Moldova (a culture, not a state). The shape stands as Cliopatria's; the found event is confidence 1. No infobox area on the pages opened.

correction.text: without Dobruja, the Roman coast where the Goths struck in 238: 'The first incursion into the Roman Empire attributable to Goths involved the sack of Histria'

keyframe_review.note: 228,826 km2, 238-246: Cliopatria adds 29 of Dobruja's 83 cells in the year of the Histria raid (Histria is a Dobruja city, my reading) and drops them in 247: a raid drawn as territory. The rest differs from the 207 outline only at the edges (about 17,000 km2 of small changes).

219,317 km2, 247-259: the Dobruja cells are gone and the shape again stops at the Danube. The Gothic king Cniva captured Philippopolis and the emperor Decius was killed 'in 250-51' (Goths page): raids south of the river that left no land.

382,367 km2 in 260: the 207 realm plus about 172,000 km2 of Pontic steppe east to the Don (37.9 E). The Greuthungi 'lived on the Pontic steppe between the Dniester and Don rivers in what is now Ukraine, in the 3rd and the 4th centuries'; the Goths page has the Chernyakhov culture 'stretch from the Danube in the west to the Don in the east' after 'the mid-3rd century'. The year 260 is Cliopatria's; no page dates the eastern growth. No infobox area.

382,343 km2, 261-269, the same outline. The decade holds the Gothic raids of the Aegean and the Balkans (the Goths page dates the battle of Naissus 'most likely' 269) and the death of Gallienus (summer 268): none left Gothic land.

634,880 km2, 270-307: adds Dacia (about 244,000 km2; 492 of its 531 cells), the year of 'Aurelian, who, however, did surrender Dacia beyond the Danube' (Goths page, 270). Caveat, soft: the page does not describe a Gothic settlement of Dacia; the Thervingi page has Eutropius saying that Dacia in 369 'now contained Taifali, Vicotali, and Tervingi', and the Thervingi first mentioned in a panegyric 'in or shortly after 291', so Dacia was shared and its Gothic share grew.

634,927 km2, 308-310: cell-identical to 270-307 (no cell added or removed); the Thervingi page places them on 'the plains north of the Lower Danube and west of the Dniester River in the 3rd and the 4th centuries'. The keyframe boundaries 308, 311, 337 and 353 are rounding differences of under 0.01 per cent.

634,903 km2, 337-352: unchanged outline. In 332 Constantine II 'decisively defeated the Goths' and Ariaric signed a treaty (Jordanes via the Thervingi page, which gives no terms); no border change is recorded.

634,857 km2, 353-372: unchanged outline. In 367 Valens 'attacked the Thervingi north of the Danube river' and in 369 made a peace 'in the middle of the Danube' (Thervingi page): a frontier fixed on the river, no land changed.

correction.text: the 353-372 outline, the Greuthungi steppe included, for 373-375: the steppe is lost to the Huns in 375 ('Around 375', Goths page; ledger) and the plains north of the Danube in 376, when the Thervingi cross the river (new keyframe gothia_376)

keyframe_review.note: 302,606 km2, 373-377: Dacia, Moldavia and Bessarabia without the steppe. Cliopatria drops the steppe in 373, but the Goths page has 'Around 375 the Huns overran the Alans' and then 'invaded the territory of the Goths', and the Alans page 'invaded the Goths in 375' (the Greuthungi page only 'in the early 370s'): the correction keeps the steppe until the 375 loss (review eu-06-a). The Cliopatria shape keeps the Thervingi plains until 377, but 'in the summer of 376, a massive number of Goths arrived on the Danube' and Athanaric 'was denied entry' (Gothic War page; the Thervingi page has Fritigern's appeal in 376).

correction.text: 'The Romans placed the Thervings along the southern bank of the Danube in Lower Moesia' after the crossing of summer 376

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Gothic shape moves to the Roman side of the river. The page gives the summer of 376 for the arrival on the Danube and no date for the placing; 376-377 is the bridge to the 378 war (Marcianople and Ad Salices are undated on the page). The north bank is Hun land from 376 (ledger).

correction.text: only the Roman lands south of the Danube: Thrace, Moesia, Dobruja and Macedonia, which the Goths raided in 378-382 and were given, 'in the provinces of Scythia, Moesia and possibly Macedonia, under their own authority', on 3 October 382

keyframe_review.note: 330,511 km2, 378-382: Cliopatria drops Moldavia and Bessarabia and adds the Balkans (about 135,000 km2) but keeps Dacia, Wallachia and Transylvania (475 Dacia cells) inside the shape, where the Huns' own shape also lies from 376. The Gothic War page records the Goths only south of the river after 376; the land is corrected to the Balkan part. In 378-382 the Thrace-Macedonia part is a contested zone (ledger), not Gothic territory.

region.text: the Dniester-Dnieper country north-west of the Black Sea, 'Scythia'

ledger.note: 207: the Goths hold the Black Sea steppe between the Dniester and the Dnieper. The year is Cliopatria's; the Goths page has Wielbark Goths 'probably in Roman service' by 200 AD and the first dated Gothic act on the Black Sea, the sack of Histria, in 238.

region.text: the Pontic steppe east of the Dnieper to the Don

ledger.note: 260: the Goths reach the Don. The Greuthungi 'lived on the Pontic steppe between the Dniester and Don rivers' in the 3rd and 4th centuries (page); the Goths page has the Chernyakhov culture reaching 'the Don in the east'. Neither page dates the growth or names the people displaced, so the year is Cliopatria's.

region.text: Dacia beyond the Danube, surrendered by Aurelian

ledger.note: 270: Aurelian gives up Dacia. 'Aurelian, who, however, did surrender Dacia beyond the Danube' (Goths page, in its 270 paragraph; the Thervingi page has the Goths 'driven back over the Danube' in the three years after 268). The page does not say the Goths settled it at once; Cliopatria's Roman shape loses Dacia in the same year.

region.text: Gothic territory north of the Danube that Valens attacked

ledger.note: 367: Valens crosses the Danube against the Thervingi. 'In 367, the Roman Emperor Valens attacked the Thervingi north of the Danube river in retribution'; the Goths retreated to the Montes Serrorum, which the page does not locate. Wallachia is my reading of 'north of the Danube'.

region.text: the Danube frontier fixed in the peace

ledger.note: 369: Athanaric makes peace with Valens in the middle of the Danube. 'In 369, Valens finally penetrated deep into the Gothic territory'; Athanaric agreed 'a peace agreement in the middle of the Danube', promising never to set foot on Roman soil.

region.text: the Greuthungi's Pontic steppe between the Dniester and the Don

ledger.note: 375: the Huns overrun the Greuthungi. 'Around 375 the Huns overran the Alans, an Iranian people living to the east of the Goths, and then, along with Alans, invaded the territory of the Goths' (Goths page); 'These Alans successfully invaded the Goths in 375 together with the Huns' (Alans page); the Greuthungi page has them 'defeated by the invading Huns in the early 370s' and Ermanaric died in 376 (Ermanaric infobox). Cliopatria drops the steppe in 373. Review eu-06-a moved this loss from 373 to 375 to match huns /ledger/2 (375).

region.text: the plains north of the Lower Danube and west of the Dniester, emptied by the crossing

ledger.note: 376: the Thervingi flee across the Danube and the plains pass to the Huns. 'In the summer of 376, a massive number of Goths arrived on the Danube', asking asylum from the Huns; Athanaric 'was denied entry'. The page does not say the Huns took the land; the huns dossier carries the matching gain.

region.text: the south bank of the Danube in Lower Moesia

ledger.note: 376: Valens lets the Thervingi settle in Lower Moesia. 'The Romans placed the Thervings along the southern bank of the Danube in Lower Moesia'; the Thervingi page has Fritigern's appeal to settle south of the river in 376 and Valens' permission. The placing itself is undated on the page.

region.text: Thrace to the Rhodope and the Hellespont, Macedonia and Thessaly

ledger.note: 378: the Goths destroy Valens' army at Adrianople and ravage the Balkans. 'On the morning of 9 August, Valens left his treasury...' (the page's year follows from its narrative); the Thervings 'went south into Macedonia and Thessaly', reaching 'as far as the Rhodope Mountains and the Hellespont'; the Greuthungi went to Illyricum and Pannonia. The revolt of 376-377 (Marcianople, Ad Salices) is undated on the page.

382: peace is declared on 3 October. 'Peace was declared on 3 October 382'; the Goths 'served as foederati' and received land 'in the provinces of Scythia, Moesia and possibly Macedonia, under their own authority'.

region.text: Scythia and Moesia on the south bank of the Danube

ledger.note: 382: the Goths' land south of the Danube becomes foederati land. 'The Goths recognized the authority of the Roman emperor and were nominally incorporated into the Roman Empire.'

region.text: the Danubian provinces of the foederati

ledger.note: 382: the Gothic realm ends as the Goths become Roman foederati. The Thervingi 'were subsequently made foederati of the Romans'; Fritigern, Alatheus and Saphrax 'are never again mentioned in the ancient histories' (Gothic War page). The Visigoths and Ostrogoths that follow are the same peoples in new states (notes).

wars.name: Gothic invasions of the Roman Empire (238-276)

zones.text: Dacia beyond the Danube, surrendered in 270

wars.outcome: Histria sacked (238); Cniva takes Philippopolis and Decius falls in 250-51; the Goths are defeated at Naissus (most likely 269); Aurelian surrenders Dacia (270); Cannabaudes' invasion after Claudius' death (270); Tacitus defeats the Goths in Asia Minor in 276.
wars.note: Only the Dacia result moved a border; the raids themselves are not drawn.

wars.name: Constantine II's war on the Thervingi (332)
wars.outcome: Constantine II 'decisively defeated the Goths' and Ariaric signed a treaty with Constantine in 332 (Jordanes via the Thervingi page); no terms or border change are given.
wars.note: The Goths page has Constantine helping the Sarmatians settle on the north bank of the Danube in 332 and about 100,000 Goths killed.

wars.name: Gothic War (367-369)

zones.text: Gothic territory north of the Danube attacked by Valens

wars.outcome: Valens attacked the Thervingi north of the Danube (367), 'penetrated deep into the Gothic territory' (369) and made peace with Athanaric 'in the middle of the Danube'.
wars.note: Valens' campaign was fought on Gothic ground; the page does not locate the Montes Serrorum.

wars.name: Hunnic invasion of Gothia (c. 373-376)

zones.text: the plains north of the Lower Danube

wars.outcome: The Greuthungi were 'defeated by the invading Huns in the early 370s'; Vithimiris and Ermanaric are gone by 376; the Thervingi crossed the Danube in 376.
wars.note: The Goths page has the Huns overrunning the Alans 'around 375'; the huns dossier carries the same war.

wars.name: Gothic War (376-382)
wars.outcome: Gothic victory: Valens killed at Adrianople (9 August 378); peace on 3 October 382 settled the Goths as foederati in Scythia, Moesia and possibly Macedonia 'under their own authority'.
wars.note: The page names Theodosius' accession (19 January 379) and the split of the Goths in 380 and dates neither the Marcianople revolt nor Ad Salices.

certainty.note: The Pontic steppe and Dacia have no recorded frontier. The Danube line is firm after 369 ('a peace agreement in the middle of the Danube') and again in the 382 foederati settlement, but both are treaty moments rather than surveyed borders.

sources.title: Goths

sources.title: Thervingi
sources.note: Territory north of the Lower Danube, 291, 332, 367-369, Dacia in 369, Fritigern in 376.

sources.title: Greuthungi
sources.note: Pontic steppe between the Dniester and the Don, kings, the Hunnic defeat in the early 370s, 376 and 386.

sources.title: Chernyakhov culture
sources.note: Countries and span of the culture (2nd-5th century), Wielbark origin, end under the Huns; thin on stage dates.

notes:
Cliopatria's 'Gothia' (207-382) is the realm of the Thervingi and Greuthungi north of the Black Sea. The Wikipedia page 'Gothia' that Cliopatria cites is a disambiguation page (Gotaland, Crimean Goths, Septimania and others), so every page here is about the Goths, Thervingi, Greuthungi, the Chernyakhov culture and the war of 376-382. A separate 'Gothia (Roman province)' page exists (a fourth-century province in Romania) and was not opened (budget).

Cliopatria shapes corrected: 238-246 draws the Histria raid as 29 cells of Dobruja; 373-377 keeps the Thervingi plains until 377 though the crossing was in 376; 378-382 keeps Dacia, Wallachia and Transylvania as Gothic although the Gothic War page puts the Goths south of the Danube after 376, and overlaps the Huns' own shape of 376-382. The new keyframe 376-377 (Lower Moesia) and the correction of 378 to the Balkans make the Goths a state inside the empire for 376-382; the Danube plains belong to the Huns from 376 (ledger loss, matched by the huns gain). The steppe loss was dated 373 here (Greuthungi page 'early 370s') and 375 in the huns dossier; review eu-06-a moved it to 375 (Goths page 'Around 375', Alans page 'in 375') and the gothia_373 correction now keeps the steppe for 373-374.

Unverified within the page budget (verdict ok): 207-237 (no page dates a Gothic presence), the eastward growth of 260 and the Gothic holding of Dacia 270-368. The Chernyakhov page gives no stage dates, no rivers and no area; no page opened has an infobox area, so the factor-of-two check was impossible.

After 382 the Thervingi continue as the Visigoths (Cliopatria's Visigoths row opens in 396 in Greece) and the Greuthungi as the Ostrogoths (Claudian's poem has 'Ostrogoths and Greuthungi' in Phrygia around 399-400, Greuthungi page); neither is a territorial successor of the 382 land, so only the Roman Empire and the Huns appear in identity.successors. Counterparts needing dossiers: the Alans of the Don (c. 370), Carpi, Taifali and Sarmatians (none in Cliopatria; no neighbours within 25 km in the seed), and the Danubian foederati kingdom of 382-395. No capital is recorded and none is given; no ruler list is given (Athanaric, Fritigern, Ermanaric, Vithimiris appear in the notes of events).
